concept: A slider is a recessed channel with a bead in it, the switch's language stretched out and lit from above. The channel fills with the loud solid up to the value, and the thumb is the same lit bead.

root.why: label and value above the channel, the order people read a setting in

head.why: the label at the start and the value at the end of one line

label.why: a visible label that is also the accessible name

value.why: the value in the measured secondary colour, with tabular figures

slider.why: the whole row is a 44px target while the channel is thin

track.why: a carved channel, shade under its top lip and light on its bottom lip

range.why: the filled part is the loud solid, white in dark and ink in light, lit at its top

thumb.why: the switch bead, lit on its top, on a short shadow

fill.why: the fill variant is one held bar: the whole pill is the track and the target

fillRange.why: the value is chosen glass, lighter than the well, lit on its top edge, its leading end rounded like the bar

fillText.why: label and value sit inside the bar at the field's inset, more than the gap between them, so the bar's edge reads as its boundary

fillLabel.why: the setting's name at the start, primary text

fillValue.why: the value with its unit at the end, tabular so it does not jitter while dragging

fillThumb.why: a thin lit bar just inside the end of the fill: the one loud mark, read rather than grabbed; it takes focus, so it carries the 44px press area

fillTrack.why: the track fills the whole well, so a press anywhere on the bar sets the value

data-disabled.why: disabled cannot move and uses the shared disabled opacity

hover.why: hover lifts the bead a little closer by growing it slightly

focus-visible.why: keyboard focus draws the shared ring with its halo, visible on any scene

@media forced-colors: active.why: forced colours drop the carve and the bead, so a real system-colour border keeps the shape

focus-within.why: the whole bar carries the focus ring, because the marker is too small to ring

active.why: while pressed the pointer shows the bar is being held and dragged

transform.why: the bead grows on hover over the hover curve

default_to_avoid.pattern: a thin grey slider rail with a blue fill and a white dot (Material slider, the browser range input)
default_to_avoid.why_not: a hairline rail on glass has no edge to find, and it shares nothing with Pane's other controls

derivation.consequence: legibility comes from dimming and blurring the backdrop (brightness, blur) inside a smoked body thick enough that a pane reads as a slab of glass, with the scene softened behind it
derivation.form: the channel is carved by dimming, shade under its top lip, light on its bottom lip

derivation.consequence: the scene supplies the hue; the system owns no hue of its own, only white at opacities and one ink, and colour appears only where it states a status or marks a diagram
derivation.form: the filled part is the loud solid, white in dark and ink in light, so the value reads without a hue

derivation.consequence: controls are full pills because they are held in the hand
derivation.form: the channel is a full pill and the thumb the switch's round bead

derivation.consequence: every target is at least 44px in its smaller dimension or has a 44px hit area
derivation.form: the channel is thin to look at but the whole row is a 44px target

variants.reason: A is Switch's material, so a settings pane with switches and sliders reads as one family (P1, P3). B adds scale marks that only help stepped values and clutter continuous ones. C's thin handle is hard to grab and breaks the round bead.

options: C A with a spectral edge
round4.reason: The user rejected the blue and showed a reference where one light from above lights every atom alike. A reads that straight: the same top rim and sheen on every surface, the white lit solid for the loud action, chosen items as lighter glass. B makes chosen items recesses, which reads as pressed-off rather than chosen. C adds a rainbow edge, a hue the system no longer owns (P1).

default_to_avoid.pattern: a thick progress bar with a round knob at its end and the label outside (Material discrete slider, web range input styled tall)
default_to_avoid.why_not: a knob on a bar the whole hand already holds is a second target, and a label outside costs a row

options: A label and value inside, thin lit marker
variants_fill.picked: A label and value inside, thin lit marker
variants_fill.reason: The user brought the reference and asked for it. A is that reference in Pane's material: well, chosen glass and one lit mark (P1, P5). B hides where the value ends on a soft fill. C suits stepped values only and clutters a continuous one. Round 3's objection to a thin handle (hard to grab) does not apply here, since the whole bar is the target.
